# github-webhook-server

> Keep GitHub pull requests moving with automated checks, approvals, labels, cherry-picks, and release workflows.

## Getting Started

- [Start Automating a Repository](quick-start.md): Set up the server, add the minimal data directory and config, connect one repository, and verify the webhook is live in minutes.

## User Guides

- [Configure Repositories](configure-repositories.md): Add repositories, choose global defaults, apply per-repo overrides, and let repository maintainers customize behavior safely.
- [Manage Pull Requests](manage-pull-requests.md): Learn what the server does automatically on PR open, review, sync, and merge so contributors understand labels, checks, approvals, and merge readiness.
- [Enable AI Features](enable-ai-features.md): Turn on conventional title suggestions, AI-assisted cherry-pick conflict resolution, and test-oracle recommendations with the sidecar and provider settings.
- [Secure Webhooks and Pull Requests](secure-webhooks-and-pull-requests.md): Protect incoming webhooks and PR automation with secrets, IP allowlists, suspicious-path detection, committer identity checks, and trusted-network-only access.
- [Debug with the Log Viewer](debug-with-the-log-viewer.md): Open live and historical webhook logs, trace PR flow by delivery ID, and inspect step-level failures when automation does not behave as expected.

## Reference

- [Configuration Reference](configuration-reference.md): Look up every supported `config.yaml` and `.github-webhook-server.yaml` key, including defaults, repository overrides, and validation rules.
